what: inkrs v0.2 on four rented cloud GPUs: an A100-SXM4-40GB (compute capability 8.0), an A10 (8.6), an L4 (8.9) and an RTX 4090 (8.9), all on the sm80 PTX tier. Per GPU: its software; the parity gates of reader-v2, hybrid_3d2d-seed42 and Reader V3 against villa eager's maps from an RTX 5090 with the default conv library and with each library forced; Hecate's parity gates against hecate.py's 5090 maps; inkrs's own 2D convolutions timed against cuDNN's (gpu-ab: 2 untimed warm-up runs, then 6 pairs in alternating order, speedup = cuDNN time / own time, so above 1 means the own convs are faster, with a 95% CI over the pairs and the noise sd of a cuDNN-against-cuDNN run with the same settings; every arm's maps were gated against the first cuDNN arm's at the villa contract); Hecate's first-run cost; and on the RTX 4090 inkrs against villa eager on the same card. Each container ran every unit in sequence on 4 vCPUs, on 2026-11-11

cudnn_algorithm_cache.note: inkrs's cuDNN algorithm cache did not load in these containers: the build these runs used keyed it on the driver release from /proc/driver/nvidia/version only, which the containers did not expose (v0.2 also asks NVML; cached_cudnn_depth0_a10 is a container where it does). Every process therefore timed cuDNN's algorithms afresh, so the cuDNN depth-0 times include a full planning in every process, and a host whose cache works replays it instead

summary.what: figures across the four GPUs, from the records below

cached_cudnn_depth0_a10.what: an A10 container of the build whose cuDNN algorithm cache keys on NVML where /proc/driver/nvidia/version is hidden; the same depth-0 benches, with every timed cuDNN arm replaying its whole plan from the cache

reader_v2_depth0.what: reader-v2 on the same segment at depth 0, both directions, 2 maps: the whole process wall, timed from outside

reader_v3_depth0.what: Reader V3 on S1 at depth 0, both directions, 2 maps: the whole process wall, timed from outside

parity.what: inkrs maps against villa eager's maps from an RTX 5090, by p1_gate.py (per map: Pearson r, p99.9 and max |diff| in 1/255 steps, identical coverage). reader-v2 on the native crop of the PHerc. 1447 segment at d -2..2, hybrid_3d2d-seed42 on S1 at d -4..4, Reader V3 on S1 at d -2..2 and stride 192 (tile 384), both directions; default means no --conv flag, inkrs and cudnn are --conv inkrs and --conv cudnn

reader_v2_default_vs_cudnn.what: the default run's reader-v2 maps against the --conv cudnn run's, byte for byte

reader_v2_pass.what: reader-v2 over the whole PHerc. 1447 segment (native, 31 x 2980 x 3240), d -2..2, both directions, stride 64, batch 64, 10 maps: the warm second sweep pass in one process

reader_v3_pass.what: Reader V3 on S1, d -2..2, both directions, stride 192, batch 8, 10 maps: the warm second sweep pass in one process

reader_v2_depth0.what: reader-v2 on the same segment at depth 0, both directions, 2 maps: the whole process wall, timed from outside

reader_v3_depth0.what: Reader V3 on S1 at depth 0, both directions, 2 maps: the whole process wall, timed from outside

hecate_first_run.what: Hecate bf16, batch 32, over the whole PHerc. 1447 segment at 9.6 um (4682 tiles in 147 batches), two processes in a row in a fresh container. Run 1 started with empty inkrs, cuDNN algorithm and CUDA driver (compiled PTX) caches; run 2 reused the driver's compiled PTX. The cuDNN algorithm cache did not load in these containers, so run 2 timed cuDNN's algorithms again. wall_s is the whole process, timed from outside; plan_s is cuDNN planning inside it

hecate_parity.what: inkrs maps against hecate.py's maps from an RTX 5090, by hecate_mapgate.py at bounds fixed before any run (fp32: r >= 0.9994, p99.9 <= 4, max <= 8 steps; bf16: r >= 0.999, p99.9 <= 6, max <= 32; mean diff on both, and no pixel 0 on one map and above 1 step on the other, while a 0 against a 1 is counted, not gated). A map whose reference has variance below 1 step squared is gated by pixels off in place of r: at most max(5, 0.01% of pixels) differ, each by 1 step. fp32 and bf16 on the 2048 x 2048 crop of the PHerc. 1447 segment, and fp32 on the edge fixture, forward and reverse
